paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God does not show favoritism. Peter says it himself in Cornelius's house: "I now truly understand that God does not show favoritism, but welcomes those from every nation who fear Him and do what is right." (Acts 10:34-35) Peter, a Jew, walked into a room full of Gentiles with a lifetime of habits telling him to stay out, and he had to learn this one standing right there. I'm telling you, if Peter needed a minute, I don't feel bad about the years it took me to learn things.

Now look at who Jesus is in all of this. Peter says Jesus Christ is "Lord of all," and that "everyone who believes in Him receives forgiveness of sins through His name." (Acts 10:36, 43) Not everyone born into the right family. Not everyone who checks every box. EVERYONE who believes. And when the Holy Spirit fell on the Gentiles while Peter was still talking, God showed that this welcome was His doing, not Peter's idea. (Acts 10:44-47)

So what does that mean for you, baker? The door into God's family is Jesus, and it's open to all who believe in Him. Nobody gets to stand at that door deciding who's good enough, and that includes you. Peter's own answer was "Stand up, I am only a man myself," so keep your eyes on the Lord of all, not on the man holding the door. (Acts 10:26)
